title: Momentum with point-in-time insider accumulation and institutional ownership
hypothesis: Proposed, not frozen: in a point-in-time dynamic liquid U.S. common-equity universe, an equal-weight rank composite of medium-term price momentum, corporate-insider accumulation and improving institutional ownership has positive net-of-cost mean daily excess return and higher independent zero-RF Sharpe than a matched momentum-only portfolio, with gains stable across chronological Development folds and later untouched evaluation windows.
rationale: Proposed economic mechanism, not an established result: momentum may reflect gradual information incorporation; publicly disclosed insider purchases may indicate management conviction; changes in disclosed institutional positions may indicate sustained demand. Their information may be complementary, but disclosure delays, crowding, confounding and trading costs could remove any incremental value.
expected_effect: Positive incremental net daily return and Sharpe for the full composite versus momentum alone. Lower volatility or drawdown alone does not confirm the return hypothesis. No unconditional promise of market outperformance or alpha.
falsification_conditions: Economic failure: full composite net mean daily excess return versus matched momentum-only is nonpositive, or its zero-RF Sharpe is no higher, in a later frozen evaluation window.
Statistical nonconfirmation: the predeclared paired moving-block excess-return test does not reject the nonpositive-effect null after Holm adjustment; lack of significance is not proof of no effect.
Robustness failure: the incremental effect is an isolated parameter optimum, dominated by one stock or regime, or disappears under predeclared cost and disclosure-delay stresses.
Incremental-information failure: the full composite adds no stable value beyond either momentum-plus-insider or momentum-plus-institutional ablation.
Design invalidation, not economic falsification: historical membership, filing availability, revisions or missingness cannot be audited point in time. Stop rather than substitute current snapshots.
confounders: Market beta, size, sector, value, liquidity and volatility exposures
Disclosure delays, reporting thresholds, transaction classification and filing amendments
Institutional holdings are reported positions, not contemporaneous fund flows
Survivorship, delisting treatment, symbol changes and present-day universe membership
Vendor backfills, revisions, stale values and nonrandom signal coverage
Momentum crashes, crowding, capacity, turnover, spread and slippage
Selection over families and parameters; modern model knowledge of historical events
asset_universe: PROPOSED: historically listed U.S. exchange-traded common equities, rebuilt at each rebalance; exact Nexus source and security-type mapping unresolved

dynamic_universe.definition: Proposed: rebuild membership at each decision using only then-listed securities, lagged price/volume and point-in-time market capitalization. Exclude ETFs, funds, preferreds, ADRs and OTC securities; retain delisted histories and corporate-action mappings. Base filters: price >= USD 5, trailing 20-session average dollar volume >= USD 10 million, market cap >= USD 1 billion. Use common audited signal coverage for matched comparisons and report coverage exclusions separately. Exact historical source, filter semantics and coverage remain UNRESOLVED; no current ticker list is a substitute. VERIFIED declaration: universe(ALL_US_STOCKS), dynamic_rebalance, filter/select_top/select_percentile and CANDIDATE binding. IsAssetType only accepts Stock/Cryptocurrency/Option/Other; Stock includes ETFs and ETF subtype is rejected locally. Historical common-equity-only membership, subtype exclusions and identifiers remain UNRESOLVED.

No explicit stock-slippage or next-session-delay argument found on inspected backtest handle; formulas/fill timing UNRESOLVED. OptionSlippageFraction is not a stock-slippage solution.

execution.event_rationale: Required to audit dynamic membership decisions, timestamped signal inputs, holdings, submitted/filled orders, costs and corporate actions. Verify that Nexus events actually expose this evidence; missing fields remain unresolved. Events must be extracted first when authorized jobs eventually complete.
execution.assumptions: Proposed long-only, unlevered, equal-weight top-N portfolio with 95% deployment and cash remainder, monthly rebalancing; weekly cadence is a declared robustness alternative. Rank each included signal cross-sectionally and average ranks with equal weights; no fitted weights, stops, leverage or interaction rules. Decisions use lagged closes and public filings; fills no earlier than the next session. Warmup is proposed calendar days, outside measured returns; Nexus warmup units/coverage, rank arithmetic, ties, scheduling, lot sizes, stale data, missing values and execution semantics require evidence. Date windows and numeric grids are provisional design choices, not coverage claims; see README.md and provenance.json. DECLARATION AUDIT: institutional 180/365 days are maximum filing recency, not summed rolling quarterly changes. Constructors verified offline only; no strategy or portfolio built. Next-session execution remains PROPOSED, not a confirmed engine setting. All PIT flags remain false.

robustness_tests: Chronological inner selection and five proposed expanding Development-only walk-forward folds with audited warmup/embargo; exact boundaries unresolved; no outer Validation tuning

Paired moving-block bootstrap of aligned daily excess returns: proposed 20-session blocks, 10000 draws, seed 2002. Proposed one-sided null-centered tests and Holm familywise alpha 0.05 across full-versus-momentum, full-versus-momentum-plus-insider and full-versus-momentum-plus-institutional in all confirmatory windows. Exact inventory and p-value implementation UNRESOLVED; existing percentile intervals do not supply adjusted p-values.
